sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2, who NC: 2024:KHC:51202 is served in the matter has remained unrepresented before this Court.

3. F.I.R. in Crime No.282/2024 was registered by Peenya Police Station, Bengaluru, initially for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC against the petitioner herein on the basis of the first information dated 02.06.2024 received from respondent No.2 herein- Ganeshraj Bansi, who is the father of the victim girl.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner and the victim girl were traced together and brought back.
The petitioner was arrested on 23.06.2024 and subsequently remanded to judicial custody.
The statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.PC was recorded on 22.06.2024 and she was also subjected to medical examination.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offence.
4. The bail application filed by the petitioner in Crl.Misc.No.8752/2024 before the jurisdictional Sessions NC: 2024:KHC:51202 Court was dismissed on 08.10.2024.

Therefore, he is before this Sanjay Kumar vs The State Of Karnataka By on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158179968/
2 Court.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is youngster aged about 20 years having no criminal antecedents.
The victim girl has stated that she had voluntarily married the petitioner and she has not made any allegation against the petitioner of he committing penetrative sexual assault against her wishes.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

6. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the bail application and submits that the victim girl is a minor and therefore, alleged offences get attracted against the petitioner and he prays to dismiss the petition.
7.

Perusal of the first information would reveal that the victim girl was found missing from her house on 29.05.2024, efforts made by her father and her relatives to trace her had failed and therefore, on 02.08.2024, her father had approached the Police and submitted first information based on which, FIR in Crime No.282/2024 NC: 2024:KHC:51202 was registered by Peenya Police Station against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC.
During the course of the investigation, the petitioner and the victim girl were traced together and the victim girl was brought back to her house.
The petitioner, who was arrested on 23.06.2024 was produced before the Jurisdictional Court and remanded to judicial custody.
8. Statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.P.C was recorded by the jurisdictional Magistrate on 25.06.2024.
The victim girl, in her statement has stated that she hails from Bihar and she was in love with the petitioner herein.
On 29.05.2024, she had gone to his house, thereafter they got married and she had stayed in the house of the petitioner along with his parents for a period of 20 days.
Her mother had given a Police complaint.
Thereafter she was subjected to medical examination and the Doctor asked her whether she had sex and she had answered affirmatively.
She has not made any allegation against the petitioner about he NC: 2024:KHC:51202 committing the act of penetrative assault on her against her wishes.
9. Petitioner is aged 20 years and his continued detention in custody is likely to have adverse impact on his future prospects.
Investigation of the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
Trial in the case is yet to commence and the prosecution has all together cited 26 charge sheet witnesses in the present case.
Therefore, chances of completion of trial in the near future is very remote.
Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the view that the petitioner's prayer for grant of regular bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

10. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is allowed.
